title: f120.4: SmtpRelayClient — raw async SMTP wire client (TLS, AUTH, DATA)
description:
Implement raw async SMTP relay client following the NntpClient pattern (crates/smtp/src/nntp_client.rs).

**What:** async fn deliver_via_relay(config, article_bytes) -> Result<(), SmtpRelayError> that connects, does TLS, EHLO, AUTH PLAIN or LOGIN, MAIL FROM, RCPT TO, DATA, QUIT.

**Algorithm:**
1. Create crates/smtp/src/relay_client.rs
2. Define pub async fn deliver_via_relay(peer: &SmtpRelayPeerConfig, envelope: &Envelope, article_bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<(), SmtpRelayError>
   - Envelope { mail_from: String, rcpt_to: Vec<String> }
3. Connection setup:
   a. tokio::net::TcpStream::connect(peer.host_port()).await (host_port = format!('{}:{}', host, port))
   b. If peer.tls: wrap with tokio_rustls::TlsConnector, use rustls ClientConfig with root CA store (use rustls::RootCertStore::from_iter(webpki_roots::TLS_SERVER_ROOTS.iter().copied())), verify server hostname. Use rustls_pki_types::ServerName::try_from(peer.host.as_str())
   c. Wrap reader/writer in BufReader/BufWriter or use tokio::io::split + BufWriter
4. Read server greeting (220 or 421) — error on anything else
5. Send EHLO {hostname} — parse response, collect extension list. On 5xx return Permanent
6. AUTH (if peer.username.is_some()):
   a. SASL PLAIN: format!("{}\0{}\0{}", authzid='', authcid=username, passwd=password) then base64-encode
   b. Send: AUTH PLAIN {encoded}\r\n
   c. If peer supports only LOGIN: send AUTH LOGIN\r\n, read 334 challenge, send base64(username), read 334, send base64(password)
   d. On 535: return Err(SmtpRelayError::AuthFailed)
   e. On 4xx: return Err(Transient(code))
   f. NEVER log the SASL-encoded string or the credentials themselves
7. Send MAIL FROM:<{mail_from}>\r\n — on 5xx Permanent, on 4xx Transient
8. For each addr in rcpt_to: Send RCPT TO:<{addr}>\r\n — on 5xx Permanent, on 4xx Transient
9. Send DATA\r\n — read 354 response
10. Dot-stuff article_bytes: for each line starting with '.', prepend extra '.'
11. Write article_bytes, then \r\n.\r\n (end of data)
12. Read final response: 250 = success; 4xx = Transient; 5xx = Permanent
13. Send QUIT\r\n (best-effort, ignore errors)
14. Return Ok(())

**parse_smtp_response(reader) -> Result<(u16, String), SmtpRelayError>:**
- Read line, enforce max 512 bytes per RFC 5321
- Parse 3-digit code, check space or hyphen continuation
- On malformed line: ProtocolError
- On 4xx: Transient; on 5xx: Permanent (return as error)
- Caller decides what is expected

**Defensive programming rules:**
- NEVER log SASL PLAIN encoded string, username, or password
- Enforce 512-byte line limit on all server responses (ProtocolError if exceeded)
- TLS: use webpki_roots for root CAs; never skip hostname verification
- Dot-stuffing: must handle lines that start with exactly '.' and preserve trailing CRLF

**Tests:** (independent oracle: RFC 5321 spec vectors)
- Test: dot_stuff() correctly adds extra '.' to line starting with '.' (oracle: RFC 5321 §4.5.2 examples)
- Test: dot_stuff() does not modify lines not starting with '.'
- Test: parse_smtp_response returns correct code for '250 OK\r\n'
- Test: parse_smtp_response returns ProtocolError for line > 512 bytes
- Test: full deliver_via_relay against tokio TcpListener mock that expects EHLO/AUTH/MAIL/RCPT/DATA sequence and returns 250 OK — confirms no credentials in mock server's received bytes

**Acceptance:**
- cargo test -p usenet-ipfs-smtp passes
- cargo clippy -p usenet-ipfs-smtp -- -D warnings passes
- dot_stuff RFC 5321 test vectors pass
- Mock server test confirms no credential logging
